svg.title: DDIA 5 · ENCODING & EVOLUTION: sketchnote
svg.text: Old and new code run side by side, so data must be readable in both directions;
and data flows through databases, services, workflows and messages.
v1 updates the name and writes the whole object back, and
phone is gone. Old code must preserve unknown fields.
Breaking changes: required fields, renumbering tags, or changing
a type in an incompatible way.
Messages: the sender doesn't wait. A broker buffers, retries,
and fans out. Producer and consumer evolve independently, so
a schema registry keeps them compatible.
Each step's result is logged. After a crash the workflow
replays: logged steps return their result, so nothing runs twice.
A broker buffers, redelivers, and fans out
Queue: one consumer per message; topic: every
"How do you deploy schema changes with zero
Expand → migrate → contract: add the nullable column,
deploy code that writes both, backfill, switch reads, and
only then drop the old column.
"How do Kafka producers and consumers evolve?"
Avro or Protobuf with a schema registry enforcing
backward-compatible changes. Consumers upgrade on their
gRPC (Protobuf, HTTP/2) for internal high-QPS calls;
REST/JSON for public APIs and browsers.
Durable workflow or saga with persisted state, plus
idempotency keys on every external call.
"Every message carries a schema version, and we only
add optional fields. That lets the booking service
deploy without coordinating with its consumers."
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.
